text:
Hospitals Test Artificial Intelligence in Radiology

A consortium of eleven hospitals has begun a two-year trial of software that analyses chest X-rays and flags those most likely to indicate disease. Radiologists would continue to examine every image, [1] the program is intended to help them prioritize urgent cases.

[2] Early results are encouraging: in a pilot at one hospital, patients whose scans were flagged as urgent received a report on average six hours sooner. Some clinicians, [3], remain wary. They worry that over-reliance on the software may erode the skills of junior doctors, and that errors in the underlying data might go [4] for years.

questions.explanation: 'Although' concedes that radiologists still examine every image, yet the program prioritizes urgent cases; the others do not fit that logic.

choices: The technology is intended to replace specialists, and to direct attention away from the images that most need it.
The technology is not intended to replace specialists, but to direct their attention to the images that most need it.
The technology was not intended to replace specialists, but to direct their attention to the images that needed it.
The specialists are not intended to replace the technology, but to direct its attention to the images that most need them.
questions.explanation: The next sentence reports early results about faster reports for urgent cases, which supports a prioritizing role; only the first option introduces that role coherently.
The clinicians' wariness contrasts with the encouraging results; 'however' marks that contrast.
Errors that 'go undetected' are not noticed; the others do not fit.

text:
Fernhill Leisure Centre – Membership Terms

Membership is offered on a twelve-month basis, and fees are payable monthly by direct debit. [1] Members who wish to cancel must give one calendar month's notice in writing; otherwise, the agreement will [2] automatically for a further twelve months.

Members may freeze their accounts for up to three months, [3] they provide evidence of illness, injury or extended travel. The centre reserves the right to vary its timetable of classes, [4] it will give at least seven days' notice of any change that affects regular sessions.

choices: The contract renews automatically at the end of each term unless cancellation has been confirmed in accordance with the procedure below.
The contract expires automatically at the end of each term unless cancellation has been confirmed in accordance with the procedure above.
The contract renewed automatically at the end of each term, whether or not cancellation had been confirmed.
The member renews automatically at the end of each term unless the centre has confirmed a cancellation fee.
questions.explanation: The next sentence explains how to cancel and what happens otherwise, so the previous one should state the renewal rule; only the first is coherent. The others contradict the renewal, use a past tense, or confuse member and contract.
An agreement 'renews' itself automatically; 'renovate' means refurbish, 'remain' needs a complement, and 'rewind' means wind back.
'Provided that they provide evidence' sets the condition; the others misstate it.
'Although it reserves the right to vary the timetable, it will give notice' concedes the right and softens it; the others do not fit.

text:
Subject: Request for a revised quotation

Dear Mr. Haddad,

Thank you for your quotation of 4 February for the supply and installation of the new security system at our Norwich warehouse. We have reviewed it carefully and consider that it compares [1] with the other proposals we have received, although the price is higher.

[2] Before we proceed, we would ask you to clarify two points. First, the quotation does not state whether the cost of maintenance is included in the stated figure. Second, [3] the delivery date you suggest falls within our busiest period, we should prefer installation to take place in March. We should be grateful if you could revise your proposal [4].

questions.explanation: An adverb is needed after 'compares': 'compares favorably with' means is as good as or better than.

choices: Your proposal is, in most respects, the one that least meets our requirements, and we would like to progress it.
Your proposal is, in most respects, the one that best meets our requirements, and we would like to progress it.
Your proposals are, in most respects, those that best meet our requirements, and we would like to cancel them.
Your proposal was, in most respects, the one that best met our requirements, and we wished to progress it.
questions.explanation: The next sentence says 'Before we proceed', so the previous one should signal intention to proceed; only the first is coherent. The others say 'least meets', cancel the proposals, or use past tenses.
'Since the delivery date falls within our busiest period' gives the reason for preferring March; 'unless' and 'whereas' do not.
'Revise your proposal accordingly' means in line with these points; 'nevertheless' and the others do not fit.
